label: paragraph_title
text: WAKE UP!

label: text
text:
extended toward certain British firms in the Colony as a result of the "past year's stagnation is wasted. Trade may not be "humming." Frankly it will take a considerable time to revert to the conditions prevailing before June of last year. But—have certain large firms and many small retail shops not missed opportunities of extending trade by the sheer pushing of British goods?
Go into any shop you like for a certain article and what is the result—you are offered a foreign article—anything but British. We may compliment others on
their commercial enterprise. But that is no reason why British firms should fill the unenviable role of mere spectators while other agents and can-vassers are mopping up all the business with the myriads of retail shops in the Colony. A personal inquiry at a Chinese store a few days ago regarding the overwhelming proportion of foreign goods and the paucity of British elicited the explanation that the others "come round and book" orders, but not so the British." Is it any wonder that British trade in the Colony is feeling the pinch? Why put all the blame for the past year's trade losses on the strike and the boycott? If one door has been closed for a time, is there no opportunity of extending trade already gained in other directions? Is there not ample scope in the confines of this Colony itself for forging ahead in business and of pushing one's wares on to the consuming public through both Chinese and non-Chinese retail shops? Has a systematic canvass ever been made with one particular line — provisions, groceries, or wearing apparel? Have British traders the faintest idea of local sales and of the proportion that goes past them into

label: text
text:
Is it not time for British traders, wholesale and retail, to wake up to their own interests and those of the Empire as a whole? Britons will never believe for a moment that the best goods come from without the Empire? Why, then, should they content themselves with bemoaning bad trade whilst doing little or nothing to extend it within their own doorstep?
The trade is here all right. It needs “going after”—that is all. Again we ask: is it not high time for the British community to wake up?—to push and to buy only British goods?

text: PIRACY CASE.

label: paragraph_title
text: WOMAN IMPRISONED FOR PERJURY.

label: text
text: Evidence for a conviction was insufficient when a fourth man (three others were recently committed for trial at the Sessions) was charged at the Central Magistracy yesterday with participation in the piracy of a fishing vessel at Lap Sap Mei, off Tai O, on May 29. He was represented by Mr. L. D. Turner.

label: text
text: FOURTH MAN GETS FREE.

label: text
text: At the close of the case the wife of one of the former defendants was sentenced to six weeks' imprisonment for committing perjury. The Magistrate remarked that her evidence did not agree with her former statements. She was remanded for a week on bail of $100 prior to serving her sentence in order that she could appear at the Criminal Sessions.

label: text
text: The woman said that whilst she and her husband were on their boat the original third defendant and another man, whom she thought was the present defendant, came on board and threatened them with a revolver and a knife. Witness rowed for some distance and the two men boarded another boat. She saw the two men again about a week later when she was offered a pair of gold bangles, which she eventually accepted in lieu of boat hire.

label: paragraph_title
text: THOMPSON MISSION

label: text
text: STIRS. IRONIC COMMENT FROM NEW YORK.

label: text
text:
New York City, July 31.
The “New York World,” in an editorial published this morning, sarcastically calls Colonel Carmi A. Thompson “an industrious lieutenant.”

label: text
text: “For wasting no time on his official mission,” the World goes on to explain, “we shall have to hand the palm to Thompson. Time has been permitted him for a three week’s survey of an archipelgo of 115,000 square miles and harbouring 3,000,000 people.”

label: text
text: "What has he discovered?" asks the paper, and replies: "First, the Philippines must grow rubber. Second, the Philippines are not ready for self-government. Third, the Filipinos don't really care much about self-government anyway."

label: paragraph_title
text: KNIGHT OF GRACE.

label: text
text:
The World then recalls the independence resolution adopted by the legislature and the action on the plebiscite bill, taken since the arrival of Colonel Thompson in the Philippines, and concludes: "Demonstrations are one thing and rubber is another. If, thanks to the right sort of laws and thanks to the right sort of capital, the Philippines turn out to be such a next little garden for growing rubber, the United States will never wish to let them go. This, however, is not Colonel Thompson's problem. Thompson is looking for facts and apparently has already found some."—United Press.
FACTS ABOUT ORDER OF ST. JOHN.

label: text
text: H.E. the Governor (Sir Cecil Clementi) having been appointed a Knight of Grace in the Order of St. John, the following may not be out of place:

label: text
text: In the Venerable Order of the Hospital of St. John of Jerusalem, the Sovereign Head and Patron is H.M. The King. The Grand Prior is H.R.H. the Duke of Connaught. The Titular Prior of the Priory for Wales is H.R.H. the Prince of Wales. The Sub Prior is the Earl of Scarborough and the Prelate is the Archbishop of York.

label: text
text: The St. John Ambulance Association and Brigade have their origin in the Order of St. John—the most ancient Order of chivalry—which was in existence at the time of the Crusades.

label: text
text: Early in the eleventh century a hospital existed in Jerusalem to minister to the needs of the Christian pilgrims who came from all parts of Europe to visit the Holy City. When in 1087 the Crusaders besieged Jerusalem, the hospice was in charge of a body of men calling themselves "The Poor Brethren of the Hospital of St. John." It was around this hospital that the Order of St. John developed.

label: text
text: Early in the nineteenth century, the English branch of the Order (which came into existence in 1130, but had been dormant since the Reformation), was revived, and in 1888 the status of the Order was confirmed by Queen Victoria, who granted a new Charter which to-day controls the work of the English Grand Priory and its departments.

label: text
text: Following the advent of the St. John Ambulance Association, there was a great advance in First Aid work, the ambulance instruction classes of the Association being especially popular in the mining areas of Derbyshire and Nottingham. In 1870 the first manual of ambulance instruction was published, and it was found necessary to establish a stores depot at St. John's Gate, from which ambulance appliances and materials could be obtained.

label: text
text: A glance at the ambulance work of the Order to-day might serve to conclude this brief survey of the history of the Order of St. John. Classes of instruction are now held by the Association in all parts of the British Empire, including such places as Bermuda, Fiji Islands, Hongkong, and British Guiana. Over 30,000 certificates are issued annually to successful candidates, in addition to about 30,000 awards to candidates who have maintained their ambulance efficiency. Classes of instruction are also held under the auspices of the Association in connection with the military and police authorities, the railway companies, the mercantile marine and the fishing fleets. Divisions of the St. John Ambulance Brigade have quickly followed the formation of Association classes, and the strength of the Brigade in the British Empire is now nearly 50,000.

label: paragraph_title
text: MURA SHIPOFF LEAVING HONGKONG.

label: text
text: APPRECIATIVE THANKS.

label: text
text: After a considerable stay in Hongkong, during which they won the approbation of a good many residents by getting over great difficulties, the Murn Shipoff Art Ballet Co. leaves tomorrow for Manila.

label: text
text: Little Miss Mura Shipoff (the baby Pavlovà) hopes to proceed to Europe to complete her education as a classical dancer. During their stay here it was hoped that a series of performances would bring forth the necessary funds but inclement weather and other circumstances were against the plucky little band of performers.

label: text
text: In connection with their departure, the following has been received:—

label: text
text: To the Editor of the “China Mail.”

label: text
text: Sir,—Mr. Lee Hy-san, proprietor of Lee Garden, has requested that you be kind enough to present the enclosed cheque to the Mura Shipoff Co., prior to their departure for Manila.

label: text
text: We had hoped to accord the company a benefit performance at Lee Garden but the weather and date of sailing have prevented our wish from being realised. In lieu thereof Mr. Lee begs that the company accept this small gift as a slight mark of appreciation of the company's praiseworthy contribution to the entertainment at Lee Garden.

label: text
text: We wish Miss Shipoff and her colleagues the best of luck in their new venture and take this opportunity of assuring them of our sincere wishes.

label: paragraph_title
text:
Thanking you, Sir,
I am, etc.,

label: paragraph_title
text:
JAS. S. MCKENZIE,
Manager,
Lee Garden.
East Point, Aug. 9:

label: text
text: In accordance with the request, the “China Mail” communicated with Mr. Arnold Stern, manager of the Mura Shipoff Co., to whom the cheque was handed to-day.

label: text
text: On behalf of his associates, Mr. Stern expressed suitable thanks to Mr. Lee Hy-san. He also takes this opportunity of telling the Hongkong community in general how grateful he and the company are for the sustained help accorded, and for the many manifestations of goodwill towards them.

label: paragraph_title
text:
THE MOTOR CAR "TOUT".
NUISANCE.

label: text
text: Sir, — Your correspondent “Chan” who takes up the cudgels on behalf of “tramp” car drivers would have us believe that the fact that they have their stands “regular or irregular” is sufficient justification for the nuisance they constitute by reason of the excessive activities of the touts.

label: text
text: I do not think that anyone objects to the existence of such cars, having regard to the fact that competition has a levelling effect on charges, but what does constitute a very real ground-for-grievance is the fact that one can never pass the Post Office-C.P.R. corner without being pestered by people who interrupt one's conversation and impede one's progress to the ferry with their continual interrogations as to whether "wanchee motor car."

label: text
text: Having suffered much at the hands of such, I seriously considered hanging notices back and front "No, I don't want a motor car" but having regard to the fact that this would cause more inconvenience than the end perhaps warranted I hit upon the scheme of informing one" persistent youngster that I wanted two motor cars, continuing my progress to my destination in the meantime. As the "lad" rose to the bait and no doubt received a

label: text
text: sengers existed only in mid-air. I have been freed from similar pesterships from that time forward. In fact, I am a marked man. And I glory in it.

label: text
text: Whether many of these touts are for cars whose rightful owners are unaware of the purpose to which the drivers are putting them I do not know. Again, that the existence of "tramp" cars as a means of competition to the cars obtainable at recognised garages does not in itself constitute a nuisance, I am prepared to admit. But everyone knows where to get such a car if he wants one and owners are only defeating their own ends by tolerating "touts" who put everybody against the practice.

label: text
text: "ANTI-TOUT." Hongkong, August 9.

label: paragraph_title
text: AGITATORS FLEE.

label: paragraph_title
text:
AVOIDING CHOLERA AT
LUTCHOW.

label: text
text: EYEWITNESS'S NOTES.

label: text
text: A correspondent who has just returned from Luichow's after spending over a week in that district reports:—

label: text
text: The local people were very friendly and practically no anti-foreign or anti-Christian spirit was manifested.

label: text
text: The agitators were either absent or on vacation. Perhaps they left when 80 per cent. of the people of Luichow city fled in terror from the epidemic of cholera that has ravaged the place for the last two months.

label: text
text: Several hundred men, women and children have died from that disease. At one time, on the main street, the only establishments that opened their doors were the Baptist Chapel, a Christian bookshop and one other shop. The epidemic is abating and the inhabitants are slowly returning.

label: text
text: The district is now entirely governed from Canton. Hongkong and Kwong-chow-wan are “under the boycott” ban yet grass mats and bags are allowed to be exported. Otherwise, trade is at a standstill and many people are suffering the pangs of hunger.

label: text
text: Luichow is a district in the southern peninsula of Kwangtung province.

label: paragraph_title
text: OUR WATER.

label: paragraph_title
text:
STORAGE FIGURES SLIGHTLY
HIGHER.
JULY STATEMENT

label: text
text: Water supplies in storage in the Colony on July 31 compare favourably with figures of the same date last year. The quantity used has decreased in Hongkong and gone up for "Kowloon. Details" follow, figures being of millions (and decimals) of gallons, except where stated:—

label: text
text: Amount in reservoirs on July 31 was 2,114.73 million gallons against 2,097.00 in 1925. Five out of six reservoirs were level with overflow as against only three last year.

label: text
text: The quantity consumed was 235.17 million gallons. Taking the population at 403,320 the average works out at 18.8 gallon per head per day. Corresponding figures for the same month last year were:—261.56 million gallons; population 393,000; average 21.4 per head per day. Last year there was a constant supply in rider main districts. This year restrictions were put in from July 7 to 18; then owing to the damage by the storm, the supply was seriously disorganised further restrictions continuing till the end of the month.

label: text
text:
Figures for Kowloon are:—
storage 451.94 million gallons
(421.94); consumption during
July 80.24 million gallons
(69.25); population 156,040
(151,000); average per head per
day 16.6 gallons (14.8). The
figures in parenthesis are those of
a twelve month ago. Full supplies
were turned on both in 1925
and 1926.

label: text
text:
The total rainfall, to July 31 (for the year) was:—1925 67.54 inches; 1926 66.78 inches.
Once again, the Colony is assured that the quality of the water, as reported on by the Government Analyst, is satisfactory.

label: paragraph_title
text: THE WEATHER.

label: text
text: For the 24 hours ending at noon to-morrow, the weather forecast is east or variable winds, moderate; fair.

label: text
text: Remarks in the Observatory report, issued at 11 a.m. to-day, are as under:

label: text
text: Pressure has decreased slightly over N.E. Japan, at Vladivostok, at Haiphong and at Legaspi. It has increased slightly from N.E. China to the Bonins and is nearly stationary elsewhere. Pressure is now over China and high over the Bonins.

label: text
text: On the trip of the R.M.S. Empress of Asia to Hongkong the passengers of the liner has been the object of several thefts, consisting of personal apparel and money. In the course of a search, a Japanese kimono, sweaters and various other personal goods, which were reported to have been lost were found in the luggage of one of the steamer's Musicians, besides cash which was found on his person. The alleged thief was arrested and was turned over to the police this morning. He will be charged tomorrow morning at the Kowloon Magistracy for larceny, if sufficient evidence is found against him.
